thread:
isabel-sales: ACME POC blocked for demo. After rotating keys they now get 401 when they include X-Redwood-Org and a new X-Redwood-Tenant header. Without headers the secret sometimes succeeds. Can we triage quickly?

ryan-eng: paste sanitized curl + last 8 of key id pls

isabel-sales: curl they ran (sanitized):
```
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED-8f7d1c2b" -H "X-Redwood-Org: acme-global" -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: acme-demo" -d '{"prompt":"status"}'
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 401 {"error":{"code":"invalid_key","message":"key not valid for requested org/tenant"}}

marta-platform: Looking up key suffix 8f7d1c2b: this is a user-scoped key created in a personal workspace. We recently rolled enforcement that rejects user keys when X-Redwood-Org or X-Redwood-Tenant is present. That matches the behavior (works w/o headers).

olivia-se: Also confirm whether the customer uses a multi-tenant header (X-Redwood-Tenant). We treat tenant binding separately from project binding; exact slug match required and case-sensitive. If the key is org-scoped but tenant is wrong you'll see a tenant_mismatch 403.

isabel-sales: They insist the key worked before rotation. Any server-side changes?

devops-bot: deploy authproxy v6.2.0 -> success (enforced tenant and org binding when headers present)

ryan-eng: We tightened checks last week to avoid cross-tenant key leakage. Recommend remediation: create an org-and-tenant scoped API key via Console (preferred) or remove tenant header for demo (temporary). Also check for mixed-deployment using old and new secrets.

marta-platform: For embeddings note: if they created a key with a preset that excludes embeddings you'll get 403 insufficient_scope for /v1/embeddings. Ask which endpoints they call.

isabel-sales: They use both generate and embeddings. They also said the rollout was gradual which might explain intermittent success.

olivia-se: If some pods still have the old personal key and others the new org key, requests with headers will fail on pods running personal key. Recommend atomic secret rollout or restart.

ryan-eng: I'll create a short-lived org+tenant scoped key (12h) with generate+embeddings and share it via secure channel for the rescue call.

devops-bot: created ephemeral key sk-org-tenant-zz12 (expires in 12h)

marta-platform: I validated ephemeral key against both endpoints with headers; both returned 200. Sending secure note to customer ahead of call. Also remind them to store secrets server-side (K8s secret/Vault) and to rotate via CI with atomic rollout.

isabel-sales: Scheduling 20-min rescue call in 30m. Can someone join to walk k8s secret rollout?

olivia-se: I'll join. Quick checklist for the call: 1) confirm key id binding in our system, 2) run generate+embed curl checks with ephemeral key, 3) verify no mixed pods (kubectl describe pods env), 4) if intermittent restart pods, 5) create permanent org+tenant key in Console and roll atomically, 6) revoke old personal keys once validated.

isabel-sales: Post-call update: we found mixed pods due to a canary rollout. We restarted the deployment, created a permanent org+tenant key in their Console with both scopes, rolled atomically, and verified /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings return 200 with headers. Customer also requested a short blurb for their security questionnaire about key storage/rotation and a ballpark price for a 2-week Dedicated eval. Looping finance. Closing thread unless new issues appear.
